data.title: Ghost Student Financial Aid Fraud — Multi-Signal Botnet Enrollment Detection
data.description: Detects ghost student financial aid fraud by correlating three botnet-driven enrollment indicators: (1) multiple FAFSA applications originating from the same device fingerprint or IP address within an enrollment cycle, (2) shared bank accounts across distinct financial aid applicants (multiple student IDs disbursing to the same routing/account number), or (3) financial aid disbursements from multiple student IDs flowing to the same beneficiary account or being withdrawn at the same ATM cluster. California community colleges flagged 31-34% of applications as potentially fraudulent, and Equifax reported preventing $180M in ghost student fraud in a single year. Ghost student botnets exploit open-enrollment admissions to submit hundreds of synthetic identity applications per cycle, file FAFSA for maximum Pell Grant eligibility ($7,395/year), and extract disbursements before census date attendance verification can trigger aid return requirements.

enrichment_required.source: Count of distinct FAFSA applications submitted from same device fingerprint within enrollment cycle
Count of distinct student IDs with disbursements to the same bank routing + account number
Count of distinct student IDs whose disbursements flow to the same downstream beneficiary
Total LMS logins by this student ID in the current term

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Ghost Student Financial Aid Fraud
// Detects shared device/IP FAFSA applications, shared bank accounts, shared beneficiaries
application_source="fafsa"
| groupBy(device_fingerprint, span=90d, function=[
    count(distinct=student_id, as=distinct_students),
    count(application_id, as=application_count),
    collect([student_id, source_ip, fafsa_submission_date, institution_id])
  ])
| distinct_students >= 3
| sort(distinct_students, order=desc)
// Parallel query for shared bank accounts
disbursement_type="financial_aid"
| groupBy([bank_routing_number, bank_account_number], function=[
    count(distinct=student_id, as=distinct_students),
    sum(disbursement_amount, as=total_disbursed),
    collect([student_id, disbursement_date, institution_id])
  ])
| distinct_students >= 2
| sort(total_disbursed, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Ghost Student Financial Aid Fraud — Shared Device Detection")`
`comment("Detects multiple FAFSA applications from same device fingerprint")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
  application_source="fafsa"
| stats dc(student_id) AS distinct_students, count AS application_count,
    values(student_id) AS student_ids, values(source_ip) AS source_ips,
    values(institution_id) AS institutions
    by device_fingerprint
| where distinct_students >= 3
| eval risk_level = case(
    distinct_students > 10, "critical",
    distinct_students > 5, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| sort - distinct_students

`comment("Splunk SPL for Ghost Student Financial Aid Fraud — Shared Bank Account Detection")`
`comment("Detects multiple student IDs disbursing to the same bank account")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
  disbursement_type="financial_aid"
| stats dc(student_id) AS distinct_students, sum(disbursement_amount) AS total_disbursed,

    values(institution_id) AS institutions
    by bank_routing_number, bank_account_number
| where distinct_students >= 2
| eval risk_level = case(
    distinct_students > 5, "critical",
    distinct_students > 2, "high",

queries.sql:
-- SQL for Ghost Student Financial Aid Fraud
-- Detects shared device FAFSA applications, shared bank accounts, and shared beneficiaries

-- Query 1: Multiple FAFSA applications from same device/IP
SELECT
  fa.device_fingerprint,
  fa.source_ip,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fa.student_id) AS distinct_students,
  COUNT(*) AS application_count,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT fa.student_id, ', ') AS student_ids,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT fa.institution_id, ', ') AS institutions
FROM fafsa_applications fa
WHERE fa.fafsa_submission_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY fa.device_fingerprint, fa.source_ip
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fa.student_id) >= 3
ORDER BY distinct_students DESC;

-- Query 2: Shared bank account across student disbursements
SELECT
  d.bank_routing_number,
  d.bank_account_number,
  COUNT(DISTINCT d.student_id) AS distinct_students,
  SUM(d.disbursement_amount) AS total_disbursed,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT d.student_id, ', ') AS student_ids,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT d.institution_id, ', ') AS institutions
FROM financial_aid_disbursements d
WHERE d.disbursement_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND d.disbursement_status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY d.bank_routing_number, d.bank_account_number
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.student_id) >= 2
ORDER BY distinct_students DESC;

-- Query 3: Cross-reference with zero academic engagement
SELECT
  d.student_id,
  d.disbursement_amount,
  d.disbursement_date,
  d.bank_routing_number,
  d.bank_account_number,
  COALESCE(l.total_logins, 0) AS lms_logins,
  COALESCE(l.assignments_submitted, 0) AS assignments
FROM financial_aid_disbursements d
LEFT JOIN lms_activity l ON d.student_id = l.student_id AND l.term = d.term
WHERE d.disbursement_status = 'COMPLETED'
  AND COALESCE(l.total_logins, 0) = 0
  AND COALESCE(l.assignments_submitted, 0) = 0
  AND d.bank_account_number IN (
    SELECT bank_account_number
    FROM financial_aid_disbursements
    GROUP BY bank_routing_number, bank_account_number
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) >= 2
  )
ORDER BY d.disbursement_amount DESC

references: Equifax Education Fraud Prevention — $180M prevented in ghost student fraud
California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office — 31-34% fraudulent application rate
DOE Office of Inspector General — Semiannual Reports on financial aid fraud
GAO, Federal Student Aid Program Integrity Reports
falsepositives: Married couples or family members legitimately sharing a bank account for financial aid from different students
Shared household devices used by multiple family members applying to the same institution
Institutional computer labs or library terminals used by multiple applicants
